business_model.claim: Adamas Trust, Inc. is an internally-managed REIT that deploys capital across credit-sensitive single-family and multi-family assets, Agency RMBS, and business purpose loan origination to generate earnings and stockholder value.
quotes: We are an internally-managed REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes focused on strategically deploying capital across complementary businesses to generate durable earnings and long-term value for stockholders through disciplined portfolio management and an operating platform designed to capture opportunities across real estate and capital markets.
Our current investment portfolio includes credit sensitive single-family and multi-family assets, as well as other types of fixed-income investments such as Agency RMBS.
Through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Constructive, we also originate business purpose loans for residential real estate investors.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, P6)
business_model.claim: The Company operates through two reportable segments: investment portfolio and Constructive.
quotes: We operate in two segments: investment portfolio and Constructive.
We derive the substantial portion of our revenues and income from our investment portfolio.

Constructive represents the mortgage origination business conducted by Constructive, a business purpose loan lender specializing in rental and transitional loans for real estate investors, which generates revenues from the origination and sale of loans.

business_model.claim: Through Constructive, Adamas originates business purpose rental and transitional loans across 48 states for residential real estate investors, retaining loans for investment or selling them to other real estate investors with certain representations, warranties, or repurchase obligations.
quotes: Constructive is a business purpose loan originator that operates in 48 states.
These loans may, from time to time, be retained on our balance sheet for investment or made available for sale to other real estate investors.

In the case of any loans originated by Constructive and sold to real estate investors, Constructive will provide the buyer of those loans with certain representations and warranties or an obligation to repurchase such loans upon certain events.

business_model.claim: Earnings and asset values are driven by interest rate shifts, yield curve changes, asset-liability reset mismatches against shorter-term borrowings, prepayment speeds, credit spreads, and borrower delinquency or default performance.
quotes: Interest rate mismatches between the interest-earning assets held in our investment portfolio and the borrowings used to fund the purchases of those assets may reduce our net income or result in a loss during periods of changing interest rates.
At the same time, certain of our borrowings provide for a payment reset period of as short as 30 days.

If short-term interest rates rise disproportionately relative to longer-term interest rates (a flattening of the yield curve), our borrowing costs may increase more rapidly than the interest income earned on our interest-earning assets.

Our credit policies and procedures may not be successful in limiting future delinquencies, defaults, foreclosures or losses, particularly in relation to declining economic conditions or significant market disruptions, or they may not be cost effective.

Tightening credit spreads generally increase the value of many of our credit sensitive assets, while widening credit spreads tend to have a negative impact on the value of many of our credit sensitive assets.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P2, P6)
business_model.claim: Because repurchase financing depends on pledged asset market values, valuation drops can force additional collateral postings or asset sales, prompting management to hedge rate and spread risks with interest rate swaps, caps, and TBA short positions.
quotes: If the market value of those assets declines, the lender may require us to post additional collateral to support the loan, as has occurred in the past, which reduces our liquidity and may limit our ability to leverage our assets.

We use swap agreements and interest rate caps as a means for attempting to fix the cost of certain of our liabilities over a period of time; however, these agreements would not be sufficient to match the cost of all our liabilities against all of our investments.
As market volatility intensified in the quarter, we proactively managed spread and convexity risks in our Agency securities portfolio through short TBA positions, lowering net Agency exposure.
